analysis.title: Global Equity Volatility Insights: The AI credit-equity disagreement
key_insights: Nasdaq fell 6.4% (-4.4σ) on 5-Nov, its worst 1-day return since the Covid drawdown. The S&P fell 4.4% (-5.6σ) and the VIX rose nearly 11.6 points. BofA reads this as a positioning-driven fragility event, not a fundamentals-driven selloff.

Three reasons for the positioning read: markets whipsawed during the week (rally on 4-Nov despite the Democratic sweep, sharp selloff on 5-Nov with no new prominent bearish headlines), the drawdown was sudden, and intra-tech dispersion after the election was near-record, with semis and memory hit hardest.

The 5-Nov S&P selloff followed a negligible overnight move, making it one of the largest open-to-close drawdowns relative to overnight returns since 2008. The VIX move was one of its largest relative to the prior day's level, similar to Feb-18 and Aug-24.

Bond yields fell sharply with equities on 5-Nov after rising overnight, so rates again treated the AI selloff as a growth shock. BofA continues to favor NDX max lookback puts contingent on lower rates as a longer-term AI downside hedge (first introduced in the 13-Oct-26 GEVI).

For the near term, BofA sees material right-tail risk in US tech despite possible post-midterm regulatory concerns. The rotation from tech into defensives is at multi-decade extremes and may reverse. Record inflows into levered semis ETFs on 5-Nov point to strong FOMO. AI regulatory stress is man-made and so reversible.

Vanilla hedge ideas: QQQ put spreads suit the near term because further weakness after a fragility shock usually grinds lower, positioning is relatively low and skew has steepened. Call spreads offer risk-limited upside hedging while equity vol is high.

Credit is repricing AI capex financing risk faster than equities. Hyperscaler bond spreads and CDS have widened materially while equity valuations and implied vols have not repriced in line. US credit strategists estimate five hyperscalers could rise from 3% of the US IG index at end-2025 to 6.3% by end-2027 if the 2026 supply pace continues.

BofA screened global AI beneficiaries for cheap equity vol versus credit spreads (z-score level and recent change versus the historical regression). The 15 largest dislocations were narrowed to an 8-name basket that minimizes basket vol: Dassault Systemes, Amazon, Meta, Nokia, SAP, SK Hynix, ASML and Alphabet.

Trade: buy a Dec27 85-65% put spread on the 8-name AI basket for 3.11% (about 6.5x max payout, implied correlation 27% on average, 42% discount to the average of individual put spreads). It gives long vol and long correlation exposure. Realized pairwise correlation is near historical lows. The long put is struck around mid-April levels. The stated risk is the premium paid.

BofA says the credit-equity disconnect can persist or widen without a catalyst. Equity vol would likely catch up quickly if leverage exposes weaknesses or fundraising pressure challenges revenue expectations. A reflexive sentiment deterioration could be enough without an earnings impact.

Asia dispersion trade: EEM 3m ATM vol is just under 30% (95th percentile of 10 years). EEM top-six realized correlation is at its 95th percentile since 2023, and implied dispersion has fallen to about 15%, near multi-year lows outside the Liberation Day episode. In Q3, realized dispersion exceeded implied by nearly 20 vol points.

Recommended trade: buy EEM top-six 3-month dispersion through ATM calls, selling EEM 3m ATM calls at 5.53% against a pro-rated basket of calls on TSMC, Samsung, SK Hynix, Tencent, Alibaba and MediaTek. Calls are preferred over straddles because dispersion is expected to be greater on the upside. Another AI selloff would lift correlations and cut the value of downside dispersion.

Risks to the Asia dispersion trade: today's correlation spike proves persistent, leaving realized dispersion low and index vol high relative to single-stock vol. The trade is not fully FX-neutral because EEM options are USD-denominated and the constituent options trade in local currencies.
Nifty's one-week rally was a 4.1σ move, among the sharpest in 20 years, as the AI trade unwound. BofA cites it as evidence that Asian markets can diverge from the AI complex.

The GFSI rose from +0.15 on 30-Oct to +0.20 on 6-Nov, the highest since 7-Apr and the 66th percentile since 2000. Thursday's one-day rise was the largest since 10-Oct-25. Equities saw the largest stress increase, Japan is the most-stressed region, and the GFSI Risk Allocator suggests a 2.4% underweight (versus 4.9% underweight on 30-Oct).

BofA's Bubble Risk Indicator (BRI) shows US healthcare and staples with extreme readings while most other major assets are below 0.5. EU Defensives basket BRI is 0.81. The SPX has 14 stocks with BRI above 0.8 (2.0% of index weight), against 50-100 stocks and 20-40% of weight at the dotcom peak.

BRI FAQ: readings above 0.8 are a rule of thumb for elevated bubble risk and tend to signal asymmetric near-term downside, but BofA treats the BRI as a cautionary tool for adding protection, not a sell signal. In eight historical bubbles, seven peaked with BRI above 0.8.

sector_views.rationale: BofA sees material upside risk to US tech from drawdown levels, with the tech-to-defensives rotation at multi-decade extremes and at risk of reversing.
Defensives show extreme bubble-like price action (high BRI), and BofA has open trades hedging high-BRI defensives with XLP and XLV put-versus-put structures against XLK.

risk_factors: Positioning-driven fragility events can repeat while elevated uncertainty exposes markets to nonlinear reflexive feedback loops.
AI regulatory pressure after the Democratic midterm sweep.
Hyperscaler debt supply could raise their share of the US IG index from 3% to 6.3% by end-2027, and funding pressure could challenge future revenue expectations.
Circular AI financing could turn idiosyncratic concerns into a systemic repricing across AI-exposed equities.
The credit-equity disconnect can persist or widen without a catalyst.
Asian correlation spike proving persistent would hurt the dispersion trade.
The BRI is price-based, can give false positives after exogenous shocks, and can miss bubbles that end quietly.

vol_and_positioning: S&P and Nikkei skew and implied vol subcomponents all saw weekly stress increases in the top deciles of their histories. Equity vol was the largest stress gainer among cross-asset vols and spreads.
Skew has steepened significantly and equity positioning is relatively low after the 5-Nov selloff.
Near-record intra-tech dispersion after the midterms, with semis and memory bearing the brunt.
SOXL (3x bull semis ETF) saw record daily inflows on 5-Nov.
Realized pairwise correlation of the AI hedge basket is near historical lows. EEM top-six realized correlation is at its 95th percentile since 2023, and implied dispersion is about 15%.
EEM 3m ATM vol is just under 30%, at the 95th percentile of the past 10 years. TWSE, Nikkei and KOSPI2 are at 98%, 97% and 97% for 10-year percentiles of 3m ATM vol.
geopolitical: US midterm elections: Democratic sweep raised questions about possible AI regulatory pressure.
Possible additional US restrictions on parts of China's AI supply chain, including optical transceivers, named as a catalyst for Asia dispersion in 2027.
Growing Chinese semiconductor competition named as a source of divergence among Asian tech names.

tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscaler equity valuations and implied vols have not repriced with wider credit spreads, and many AI beneficiaries are cash generative with net cash positions.
tension_points.bear_case: Credit is signaling AI financing strain. Equity vol would likely catch up quickly if leverage exposes vulnerabilities or fundraising pressure challenges revenue expectations, and a reflexive sentiment deterioration could be enough.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The disconnect can persist or widen while vulnerabilities stay latent and no catalyst emerges, which would hurt the long-vol basket trade through carry cost.

tension_points.bull_case: Material right-tail risk remains in US tech: the rotation into defensives is at multi-decade extremes, FOMO shows in record levered semis ETF inflows, and AI regulatory stress is man-made and reversible.
tension_points.bear_case: Further weakness after a fragility shock typically grinds lower, and post-midterm AI regulation could pressure the AI boom.
